SPACE CRAFT JOURNAL / FIT-OUT & RENOVATION

Office renovation services how to create a workspace.

Understand the existing space before changing it. This Space Craft planning note looks at office renovation services how to create a workspace through the choices that affect everyday use, the details worth testing and the questions to take into your project brief.

Space Craft editorialPlanning note · 4 min read
IN THIS NOTESurvey before setting the scopeMake dependencies visiblePlan the move and the handoverMap activity before assigning desksBefore you decide
01 / DESIGN CONSIDERATION

Survey before setting the scope

Record the condition of the space, fixed services and any building requirements. Discuss which elements can be retained, adapted or removed before developing a new finish scheme.

02 / DESIGN CONSIDERATION

Make dependencies visible

Some work needs approval, specialist coordination or a sequence of activities. Discuss these dependencies when planning the programme rather than treating the desired date as the only input.

03 / DESIGN CONSIDERATION

Plan the move and the handover

If the office remains in use, consider phasing, access and disruption. Agree review points, snagging and the information needed to operate the space after completion.

04 / DESIGN CONSIDERATION

Map activity before assigning desks

Write down the tasks people perform, how often teams overlap and when visitors arrive. A desk count alone will not reveal the need for private calls, project tables or storage.

BEFORE YOU DECIDE

Take this into your brief.

  • Gather existing drawings and building requirements.
  • Record what stays and what changes.
  • Discuss access, phasing and handover with the project team.

Write down one priority, one constraint and one question you still need to answer. Review them beside the plan or material sample before agreeing the next design decision.
